links.outcome: Sensitivity, specificity, recall, and workload when radiologists evaluate AI-negative cases versus AI alone
links.effect: Strategy 4 (radiologist evaluation of AI-negative cases) matched sensitivity (0.956 vs. 0.991), improved specificity (0.787 vs. 0.698), cut workload 54.5%, and decreased recall and false positives.
links.quote: It not only matched the high sensitivity of original algorithm (0.956 vs. 0.991) but also improved specificity (0.787 vs. 0.698), reduced radiologist workload by 54.5%, and decreased both recall and false positive rates.

links.outcome: Human-AI collaborative strategies versus standalone AI performance in HCC ultrasound screening
links.effect: Strategy 4 combining AI detection with radiologist review of negatives outperformed other strategies; specificity 0.787 vs 0.698 for original algorithm, sensitivity 0.956 vs 0.991.
links.quote: Among the strategies tested, Strategy 4, which combined AI for initial detection and radiologist evaluation of negative cases in both detection and classification phases, outperformed others.

unlisted_practices: Human-AI collaborative triage in which AI-negative cases are routed to radiologists to reduce workload
